subject: Mathematics
title: Priya's Chocolate Cake Party
hook: Priya bakes a cake, cuts it into pieces, and learns fractions and decimals by sharing with friends.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: bakes cakes and discovers fractions through sharing

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: helps measure recipe ingredients and split portions

slides.title: The Birthday Cake Bake
slides.storyContext: Priya bakes a big chocolate cake for her birthday. She cuts it into 8 equal slices. Arjun eats 2 slices. What fraction did he eat?

points.label: Setup
points.text: One whole cake, 8 equal pieces, Arjun takes 2 pieces

slides.inSimpleWords: Fractions show parts of something whole.

image.alt: The Birthday Cake Bake — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Understanding Fractions
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: the bottom number (8) tells you how many equal parts. The top number (2) tells you how many parts Arjun got.

points.label: Numerator (top)
points.text: 2 — the pieces Arjun got

points.label: Denominator (bottom)
points.text: 8 — total equal slices

points.label: Fraction
points.text: 2/8 (two-eighths) of the cake

slides.inSimpleWords: Top = parts taken, bottom = total parts.

image.alt: Understanding Fractions — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Fractions in Real Cakes
slides.storyContext: Priya cuts another cake into halves (2 parts). Arjun eats 1 half. She cuts a third cake into quarters (4 parts) and Arjun gets 1 quarter.

example.problem: Name the fractions: 1 half, 1 quarter, 2 halves

slides.inSimpleWords: Halves, thirds, quarters are common fractions.

image.alt: Fractions in Real Cakes — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Comparing Fractions
slides.storyContext: Priya has 1/4 cake left. Arjun has 1/2 cake left. Who has more?

points.label: Same numerators
points.text: 1/4 vs 1/2 — smaller denominator = bigger piece
Half is bigger than a quarter

points.label: Tip
points.text: Smaller bottom number = bigger actual piece

slides.inSimpleWords: Smaller bottom means a bigger slice.

image.alt: Comparing Fractions — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Intro to Decimals
slides.storyContext: Arjun measures milk for the frosting: 0.5 litres (half a litre) and 0.25 litres (a quarter). Decimals use points, not fractions!

points.label: Decimal point
points.text: The dot (.) separates whole from parts
Same as 1/2 (five-tenths)
Same as 1/4 (twenty-five hundredths)
One-tenth of a whole
One-hundredth of a whole

slides.inSimpleWords: Decimals show parts using a point.

image.alt: Intro to Decimals — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Fractions and Decimals Together
slides.storyContext: Priya reads a recipe: 3/4 cup sugar (same as 0.75 cup). She uses 1/2 cup flour (same as 0.5 cup). Arjun writes both ways.

example.problem: Write as both fraction and decimal: 3/4, 1/2, 1/10

slides.inSimpleWords: Fractions and decimals are two ways to say the same part.

image.alt: Fractions and Decimals Together — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: The Cake Sharing Problem
slides.storyContext: Priya bakes 3 cakes. Each has 8 slices. She gives 2/8 to Arjun, 3/8 to a friend, and keeps 1/8. How many slices are left unsold?

points.label: Problem
points.text: Total 24 slices. 2/8 + 3/8 + 1/8 = 6/8. How many remain?

slides.inSimpleWords: Add fractions and subtract from the total.

image.alt: The Cake Sharing Problem — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: The Party Success
slides.storyContext: Priya's birthday party is perfect. Everyone gets a fair share: Arjun gets 1/4, friend gets 1/3, family gets the rest. Fractions made sharing fair and fun!

points.label: Lesson
points.text: Fractions and decimals help us divide, measure, and share wisely in everyday life

slides.inSimpleWords: Fair sharing needs fractions and decimals.

image.alt: The Party Success — Fractions and Decimals

slides.title: Fractions & Decimals Recap
slides.storyContext: Priya and Arjun recap their delicious discovery.

points.label: Fractions
points.text: Top = parts taken, bottom = total parts (e.g., 2/8)

points.label: Common fractions
points.text: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 3/4 appear everywhere

points.label: Decimals
points.text: Use a point: 0.5, 0.25, 0.75 = same as fractions

points.label: Use it
points.text: Cooking, measuring, sharing, money

slides.inSimpleWords: Fractions and decimals split whole things fairly.

image.alt: Fractions & Decimals Recap — Fractions and Decimals

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun's Garden Design
hook: Arjun designs a school garden using rectangles, circles, and triangles, then builds 3D structures.

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: plans the garden layout using shapes and angles

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: calculates area and perimeter for planting

slides.title: The Garden Plan
slides.storyContext: The school wants a beautiful garden. Arjun is in charge of design. He uses a big rectangle for the main plot, circles for flower beds, and triangles for shade structures.

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Draw and measure shapes to use space wisely

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes help plan and build gardens.

image.alt: The Garden Plan — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: 2D Shapes: Sides and Angles
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Arjun about flat (2D) shapes: a rectangle has 4 sides and 4 right angles (90°). A triangle has 3 sides and 3 angles.

points.label: Rectangle
points.text: 4 sides, 4 right angles (90°), opposite sides equal

points.label: Triangle
points.text: 3 sides, 3 angles, many types (right, equilateral, isosceles)

points.label: Circle
points.text: No sides, no angles, all points same distance from centre

points.label: Square
points.text: Special rectangle: 4 equal sides, 4 right angles

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes have sides and angles.

image.alt: 2D Shapes: Sides and Angles — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Calculating Perimeter
slides.storyContext: Arjun's main garden plot is a rectangle: 8 metres long, 5 metres wide. He needs to fence it. How much fencing does he need?

example.solution: Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(8+5) = 2(13) = 26 metres of fencing needed

slides.inSimpleWords: Perimeter = add all the sides.

image.alt: Calculating Perimeter — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Calculating Area
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: how much soil do we need for the garden? We measure the AREA (space inside), not just around it.

points.label: Area of rectangle
points.text: length × width = 8 × 5 = 40 square metres

points.label: Area of square
points.text: side × side; for 5m side: 5 × 5 = 25 square metres

points.label: Area of triangle
points.text: 1/2 × base × height

points.label: Square metres
points.text: Unit for measuring area (m²)

slides.inSimpleWords: Area = space inside a shape.

image.alt: Calculating Area — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Designing Flower Beds
slides.storyContext: Arjun designs three flower bed shapes: a square (4m × 4m), a triangle (base 6m, height 4m), and a circle (radius 3m).

example.problem: Find the areas: Square 4×4, Triangle base 6 height 4, Circle radius 3
example.solution: Square: 4×4=16 m²; Triangle: 1/2×6×4=12 m²; Circle: 3.14×3²≈28 m²

slides.inSimpleWords: Different shapes need different area formulas.

image.alt: Designing Flower Beds — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: 3D Shapes (Objects with Volume)
slides.storyContext: For shade, Arjun plans a small hut. That's a 3D shape! A cube (box), a cone, and a cylinder are common 3D shapes.

points.label: Cube
points.text: 6 square faces, 8 corners, all sides equal (dice shape)

points.label: Cuboid (box)
points.text: 6 rectangular faces, length, width, height differ

points.label: Sphere
points.text: Ball-shaped, no flat faces, no corners

points.label: Cylinder
points.text: Two circular faces, curved surface (tin can shape)

points.label: Cone
points.text: One circular base, one point at top (ice cream cone)

slides.inSimpleWords: 3D shapes have volume (thickness).

image.alt: 3D Shapes (Objects with Volume) — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: The Garden Structure
slides.storyContext: Arjun's shade hut is a cube with 2m sides. He needs to know the volume (how much air inside). What's the volume?

points.label: Problem
points.text: A cube hut: 2m × 2m × 2m. What's the volume?

example.problem: Volume of a cube with 2m sides = ?
example.solution: Volume = side × side × side = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cubic metres (m³)

slides.inSimpleWords: Volume = space inside 3D shapes.

image.alt: The Garden Structure — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: The Garden Grand Opening
slides.storyContext: The garden is built! A rectangle of soil (40 m²), circle flower beds (28 m²), triangle shade areas, and a cube hut (8 m³). Arjun's geometry design is perfect!

points.label: Success
points.text: Geometry made the garden beautiful, organized, and functional

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes turn plans into real gardens.

image.alt: The Garden Grand Opening — Geometry Shapes

slides.title: Geometry Mastered
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya celebrate their shape skills.

points.label: 2D shapes
points.text: Rectangles, triangles, circles (flat, no thickness)

points.label: Perimeter
points.text: Distance around a shape

points.label: Area
points.text: Space inside a shape (square metres)

points.label: 3D shapes
points.text: Cubes, spheres, cylinders (have volume)

points.label: Use it
points.text: Building, designing, planning, architecture

slides.inSimpleWords: Geometry helps us design and measure our world.

image.alt: Geometry Mastered — Geometry Shapes

subject: Science
title: Arjun's Space Adventure
hook: Arjun and Priya zoom through the solar system and visit each planet to learn about our cosmic neighbourhood.

characters.name: Priya
characters.role: navigator with a star map and endless questions

slides.title: Blast Off to Space!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya hop into a rocket at Earth's south pole. They're heading to explore the eight planets orbiting our Sun.

points.label: Setting
points.text: A spacecraft in orbit, with Earth and the Sun visible below

slides.inSimpleWords: The solar system is our home in space.

image.alt: Blast Off to Space! — The Solar System

slides.title: The Sun: Heart of Our System
slides.storyContext: The Sun is enormous, burning hot, and everything orbits it! Arjun feels the warmth even from this distance.

points.label: The Sun
points.text: A giant ball of burning gas (star), gives light and heat

points.label: Size
points.text: 109 times wider than Earth; we could fit 1.3 million Earths inside!

points.label: Energy
points.text: All life on Earth depends on the Sun's energy

points.label: Age
points.text: About 4.6 billion years old (middle-aged for a star)

slides.inSimpleWords: The Sun is a giant fire ball that rules our system.

image.alt: The Sun: Heart of Our System — The Solar System

slides.title: The Eight Planets
slides.storyContext: Priya points to her star map. There are 8 planets, ordered by distance from the Sun. Mercury is closest and hottest; Neptune is farthest and coldest.

points.label: Close planets
points.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (small, rocky, inner)

points.label: Far planets
points.text: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune (huge, icy or gassy, outer)

points.label: Earth
points.text: Our home! Just right for life (water, air, perfect temperature)

points.label: No Pluto
points.text: Pluto was demoted to a 'dwarf planet' in 2006

slides.inSimpleWords: Eight planets orbit the Sun in order.

image.alt: The Eight Planets — The Solar System

slides.title: Mercury to Mars: The Inner Planets
slides.storyContext: Arjun's ship zooms past the inner rocky planets. Mercury is tiny and scorching (450°C!). Venus is thick with clouds. Earth is perfect. Mars is red and cold.

example.problem: Why is Earth special but Mercury and Venus are not?
example.solution: Earth has liquid water, breathable air, and moderate temperature. Mercury is too hot, Venus's atmosphere crushes everything.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rocky planets near the Sun are too harsh for Earth life.

image.alt: Mercury to Mars: The Inner Planets — The Solar System

slides.title: The Gas Giants: Jupiter and Saturn
slides.storyContext: Priya sees Jupiter, the HUGE gas giant with red storms. Then Saturn, with its beautiful rings made of ice and rock.

example.problem: Jupiter is 11 times wider than Earth. How many Earths fit inside Jupiter?
example.solution: About 1,300 Earths fit inside Jupiter! (volume is 11³ times bigger)

slides.inSimpleWords: Gas giants are enormous, not solid, with many moons.

image.alt: The Gas Giants: Jupiter and Saturn — The Solar System

slides.title: The Moon: Earth's Faithful Friend
slides.storyContext: As they return, Arjun and Priya orbit Earth and marvel at the Moon. It orbits Earth, causes tides, and lights our night sky.

points.label: The Moon
points.text: Earth's natural satellite, orbits us every 27 days

points.label: Tides
points.text: Moon's gravity pulls Earth's oceans, creating high and low tides

points.label: Phases
points.text: New moon, crescent, half moon, full moon (Earth sees different lit parts)

points.label: Distance
points.text: About 384,000 km away (still our nearest neighbour)

slides.inSimpleWords: The Moon dances around Earth every month.

image.alt: The Moon: Earth's Faithful Friend — The Solar System

slides.title: Asteroid Belt Mystery
slides.storyContext: Between Mars and Jupiter, millions of rocks float in an asteroid belt. Priya asks: how did this belt form?

points.label: Challenge
points.text: The asteroid belt might be pieces of a planet that never formed. Why?

example.problem: What might have prevented a planet from forming in the asteroid belt?
example.solution: Jupiter's strong gravity scattered and prevented rocks from clumping together to form a planet.

slides.inSimpleWords: The asteroid belt is cosmic rubble.

image.alt: Asteroid Belt Mystery — The Solar System

slides.title: Home Sweet Earth
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya land back on Earth. Looking up at the night sky, they see the Moon and planets they visited. Earth suddenly feels precious and unique.

points.label: Realization
points.text: Our planet is a rare jewel in a vast solar system

slides.inSimpleWords: Earth is special, and we must care for it.

image.alt: Home Sweet Earth — The Solar System

slides.title: The Solar System Recap
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya chart their adventure and what they learned.

points.label: The Sun
points.text: Giant star at the centre, gives light and heat

points.label: 8 Planets
points.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (inner rocky); Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune (outer giant)

points.label: The Moon
points.text: Earth's satellite, causes tides, lights the night

points.label: Why Earth?
points.text: Water, air, right temperature = perfect for life

points.label: Explore
points.text: There is so much more to discover in space!

slides.inSimpleWords: The solar system is our cosmic home to explore.

image.alt: The Solar System Recap — The Solar System
